h: Knife wound piercing left lung and left ventricle: entry site?
p: The cardiac apex lies in the left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line, with the left lung overlying the heart.

h: Chromaffin-cell mass beside the IVC: which hormone does it secrete?
p: Extra-adrenal chromaffin tumors (paragangliomas/pheochromocytoma) secrete catecholamines, mostly norepinephrine; confirm with plasma metanephrines.

h: Alternating-side headaches with photophobia, phonophobia and nausea: diagnosis?
p: Recurrent unilateral or alternating throbbing headache with nausea, light and sound sensitivity; estrogen-containing contraceptives can worsen migraine with aura.

h: Pregnant woman: pink sticky discharge from one nipple, no mass: diagnosis?
p: Intraductal papilloma is the most common cause of bloody or serosanguinous unilateral nipple discharge in women of reproductive age; mastitis is painful and erythematous.

h: Intern berates a student after being criticized by a superior: defense mechanism?
p: Displacement redirects emotion from a threatening target to a safer one (kick the dog); projection attributes one's own feelings to others.

h: M3 muscarinic agonist: intracellular signaling?
p: M1, M3 and M5 are Gq-coupled (PLC, IP3, DAG, calcium). M2 is Gi-coupled, slowing the heart by increasing K+ conductance.

h: Genetic variant protecting against falciparum malaria in endemic Africa?
p: HbS (Glu6Val) and HbC (Glu6Lys) heterozygosity protect against P. falciparum; G6PD deficiency and thalassemia also confer some protection.

h: Serum sickness after TMP-SMX: expected complement level?
p: Type III hypersensitivity: immune complexes activate and consume complement (low C3 and C4), causing fever, rash, arthralgia and vasculitis 1-2 weeks after exposure.

h: Musty odor, seizures, fair skin in infant: amino acid to supplement?
p: Phenylketonuria (phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency) makes tyrosine essential; treat with low-phenylalanine diet plus tyrosine.

h: Anterior duodenal ulcer: greatest complication risk?
p: Anterior duodenal ulcers perforate (free air under the diaphragm); posterior ulcers erode the gastroduodenal artery and bleed.

h: Xanthelasma on the eyelids: first blood test?
p: Xanthelasma are cholesterol deposits and suggest hyperlipidemia (familial or secondary); a lipid panel is the initial test.

h: 2 weeks of purulent nasal discharge, headache, postnasal drip in a child: diagnosis?
p: Persistent URI symptoms beyond 10 days (or double worsening) suggest bacterial sinusitis; colds resolve within about a week.

h: Tumor cells with decreased MHC I: which cell kills them?
p: NK cells attack cells lacking MHC I ('missing self'); cytotoxic T cells need MHC I presentation.

h: Shellfish ingestion with perioral tingling then paralysis: toxin mechanism?
p: Saxitoxin (paralytic shellfish poisoning) and tetrodotoxin block voltage-gated Na+ channels. Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins (syntaxin, SNAP-25).

h: Machine-like murmur in an infant: drug to close the ductus?
p: PDA gives a continuous machinery murmur; NSAIDs (indomethacin, ibuprofen) inhibit prostaglandins to close it. PGE1 keeps a ductus open.

h: Obsessions with washing rituals: most effective treatment?
p: OCD: exposure and response prevention (CBT) plus an SSRI, often at higher doses; clomipramine is second line.

h: Antiepileptic causing bilateral acute angle-closure glaucoma?
p: Topiramate (also sulfonamide-related) can cause acute angle-closure glaucoma and myopia, plus kidney stones, metabolic acidosis and weight loss.

h: Nondepolarizing paralytic that causes histamine-release hives and hypotension?
p: d-Tubocurarine and atracurium trigger mast-cell histamine release, causing hypotension, flushing and bronchospasm.

h: First-trimester chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria: treatment?
p: Doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy (teeth and bone effects), so quinine is paired with clindamycin in the first trimester. Check current local guidance, which has evolved.

h: Two n+1 and two n-1 gametes: stage of nondisjunction?
p: Meiosis I nondisjunction makes all four gametes abnormal (two n+1, two n-1). Meiosis II errors give normal gametes alongside abnormal ones.

h: Hydroxyurea in sickle cell disease: which cell cycle phase is blocked?
p: Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, halting DNA synthesis; it raises HbF and causes macrocytosis.

h: Flaccid blisters, oral erosions, skin separates on rubbing: disrupted protein?
p: Pemphigus vulgaris: IgG against desmoglein 3 (cadherin) causes acantholysis. Bullous pemphigoid targets hemidesmosomes (collagen XVII).
